analysis.investment_thesis: IGI operates a gemological certification business with genuine moat characteristics — trusted brand, network effects between jewellers and consumers, high switching costs, and near-zero marginal cost per additional certificate — producing ROE of 43% and ROCE of 54% with minimal capital needs. However, the recent PE-backed IPO, only three years of public data, and PE sponsor exit risk temper my enthusiasm despite excellent business fundamentals.
key_strengths: Business model resembles a ratings agency or standards bureau: certification trust compounds over decades, margins are exceptional (56% operating, 77% gross), and capex is negligible (INR 63 Cr on INR 1,229 Cr revenue)
Consistent and growing free cash flow — INR 439 Cr FCF in FY25, 100% OCF positivity across all four years of data, with revenue CAGR of 35.8%
Dual tailwind: natural diamond certification growing with Indian jewellery market, and lab-grown diamonds represent an entirely new and fast-growing certification revenue stream
key_risks: GIA (Gemological Institute of America) dominates global prestige diamond certification; IGI competes on price and accessibility but lacks GIA's top-tier brand in the high-value segment
Three-year data track record is insufficient to assess full-cycle durability — I cannot see how this business performed in a jewellery demand recession
Lab-grown diamond boom could be a double-edged sword: volume grows but per-certificate fees may compress as LGD becomes commoditised
red_flags: PE-backed IPO: parent is BCP Asia II TopCo Pte. Ltd. (Blackstone). Promoters hold 76.55% — PE sponsors at IPO typically price deals to capture maximum value for themselves, not incoming shareholders
Negative equity in FY23 (-INR 604 Cr) signals a pre-IPO leveraged dividend recapitalisation by PE sponsors — they extracted cash before listing investors, a practice I find deeply unflattering
P/B of 11.44x and P/S of 13.11x leave thin margin of safety; any slowdown in India's jewellery demand or diamond market would expose this valuation quickly
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The IGI business model genuinely excites me in principle. Certification and accreditation businesses are among the most durable franchises in capitalism — think of the value embedded in a trusted hallmark. With 83% of revenue converted to EBITDA and virtually no capex burden (INR 63 Cr capex vs INR 502 Cr operating CF in FY25), this is an extraordinarily capital-light compounder. The FY22-FY25 revenue CAGR of 35.8% is impressive, though it partly reflects India's post-COVID jewellery boom and the explosion of lab-grown diamond volumes.

My caution is primarily about provenance and price. The negative equity in FY23 — driven by a PE dividend recap before the IPO — tells me Blackstone extracted significant value before public investors arrived. The IPO in late 2024 raised INR 1,188 Cr in financing inflows, coinciding with the equity restoration. I have seen this pattern before: PE sponsors sell businesses at peak multiples, leaving public shareholders with less upside and more risk. P/B of 11.44x and P/E of 30x are not unconscionable for this quality, but they leave me with an inadequate margin of safety given the limited track record. I would want to observe 2-3 more years of results — especially through a diamond market correction — before buying at scale.
